El 26 de mayo de 2023, el usuario trabajó en una propuesta para NEST Student Co-Living, una plataforma de alojamiento temporal para estudiantes universitarios que buscan vivienda cerca de sus universidades. NEST se dirige a estudiantes jóvenes, tanto locales como extranjeros, y conecta estudiantes con propietarios y compañeros de vivienda mediante una prueba de compatibilidad que considera factores como presupuesto y ubicación.

La propuesta de NEST plantea que la plataforma ayuda a propietarios con viviendas cerca de universidades a encontrar estudiantes para alquileres de corto plazo, potencialmente generando ingresos de propiedades que de otro modo podrían estar vacías o resultar costosas de mantener. Para los estudiantes, NEST ofrece opciones temporales a precios razonables y ayuda a encontrar propietarios y compañeros de vivienda compatibles.

On 2023-05-26, the user supplied definitions for 35 variables in an H1N1 survey dataset. Concern about H1N1 (h1n1_concern) is coded 0=not at all, 1=not very, 2=somewhat, 3=very concerned; H1N1 knowledge (h1n1_knowledge) is 0=no knowledge, 1=a little, 2=a lot. Eight vaccine-opinion variables use ordered five-category scales: opinion_h1n1_vacc_effective and opinion_seas_vacc_effective (1=not at all effective, 2=not very effective, 3=don't know, 4=somewhat effective, 5=very effective); opinion_h1n1_risk and opinion_seas_risk (1=very low, 2=somewhat low, 3=don't know, 4=somewhat high, 5=very high risk without vaccination); opinion_h1n1_sick_from_vacc and opinion_seas_sick_from_vacc (1=not at all worried, 2=not very worried, 3=don't know, 4=somewhat worried, 5=very worried about becoming sick from vaccination).
records.topic: H1N1 survey variable definitions and coding

records.text: The user defined these 13 H1N1 survey variables as binary: behavioral_antiviral_meds (taken antiviral medications); behavioral_avoidance (avoided close contact with people with flu-like symptoms); behavioral_face_mask (bought a face mask); behavioral_wash_hands (frequently washed hands or used hand sanitizer); behavioral_large_gatherings (reduced time at large gatherings); behavioral_outside_home (reduced contact with people outside the household); behavioral_touch_face (avoided touching eyes, nose, or mouth); doctor_recc_h1n1 (doctor recommended H1N1 vaccine); doctor_recc_seasonal (doctor recommended seasonal flu vaccine); chronic_med_condition (has at least one of the specified chronic conditions, including lung disease/asthma, diabetes, heart or kidney condition, anemia, neurological/neuromuscular or liver condition, or chronic-illness/medication-related weakened immunity); child_under_6_months (regular close contact with a child younger than six months); health_worker (is a healthcare worker); health_insurance (has health insurance).

The user defined demographic and residence variables in the H1N1 survey: age_group (respondent age group), education (self-reported education), race, sex, income_poverty (household annual income relative to 2008 Census poverty thresholds), marital_status, rent_or_own (housing situation), employment_status, hhs_geo_region (residence in a 10-region U.S. Department of Health and Human Services classification, with values represented by short random character strings), and census_msa (residence within a Census-defined metropolitan statistical area).
records.topic: H1N1 survey demographic and geographic variables

records.text: The user defined household and employment variables in the H1N1 survey: household_adults is the number of other adults in the respondent's household, top-coded at 3; household_children is the number of children in the household, top-coded at 3; employment_industry and employment_occupation indicate the respondent's industry and occupation, with values represented by short random character strings.

On 2023-05-26, the user asked how to research effectively for a term paper and said they often feel overwhelmed by the amount of information available.
The user plans to begin narrowing a term-paper topic by brainstorming a list of ideas, and is considering discussing those ideas with a professor or librarian.

Advice given for effective term-paper research included forming a clear research question, using credible academic sources and library databases, taking notes, tracking citation details, planning research time, and organizing sources into subtopics and an outline. Advice for narrowing a topic included brainstorming, clarifying the paper’s purpose and scope, reviewing recent research for gaps, and developing a focused research question. Discussing ideas with a professor or librarian was recommended for guidance, resources, focus, feasibility, and avoiding pitfalls.
